name: xgo-uniform-structural-child-edges-for-every-node
instr:
XGo lacks a uniform view of ordered structural children across ordinary, query, compiler-proxy, and template AST nodes. Add child edges with their owning role and list position without changing parsing, walking, printing, compilation, or outlining behavior.

Each child-edge sequence must be deterministic and side-effect free. Include every syntactic child exactly once in declared field and list order. Omit absent and typed-nil children, but preserve present zero-position nodes and meaningful empty aggregates. `ChildRole` in both `github.com/goplus/xgo/ast` and `github.com/goplus/xgo/tpl/ast` is string-backed. `NoChildIndex` from `github.com/goplus/xgo/ast` is exactly `-1`.

Make `ast.Walk` follow `Node.ChildEdges` while preserving its depth-first order, pruning behavior, and trailing nil callbacks. Make `gopq.Node.ChildEdges`, `Child`, and `Any` expose the curated `ForEach` hierarchy consistently. Recursion is preorder, and `ErrBreak` stops immediately before later siblings become observable. Direct edges from parsing a file must agree with gopq Child and Any's recursive preorder.

Compiler proxy edges expose only the currently effective identifier, including after copy-on-write renaming, without changing spans or compilation results. Template edges preserve grammar order and cross exactly once from a Rule's optional RetProc into ordinary AST children.

Complete and recoverable partial parser results must be immediately safe to traverse without changing returned file and erro
